A cleaning is a hygiene appointment, and cancelling 24 hours before the appointment is less than the required 48-hour notice [3], so this counts as a late cancellation. The late cancellation fee for a hygiene appointment is **$35** [1].

Just a reminder: the fee can be waived once per patient per calendar year at the front desk's discretion, and it's always waived for medical emergencies or county-declared severe weather [1].
Our office is located at 410 Heron Lake Blvd, Suite 200, Kissimmee, FL 34741 [1].

**SunCoast PPO patient – Yes, they can come back on October 1.**
SunCoast PPO allows 2 cleanings per calendar year and does **not** require a 6-month gap between visits; it simply counts toward the calendar-year limit [1]. Since the May 1 cleaning was their first of the year, an October 1 cleaning would be their second and is within the plan's frequency [1].

**BlueWave HMO patient – No, October 1 is too soon.**
BlueWave HMO requires cleanings to be at least **6 months apart** [4]. May 1 → October 1 is only **5 months**, so the visit would not yet meet the interval requirement [4]. If the patient still wants to be seen on October 1, the front desk must inform them of the self-pay fee of **$120 for an adult cleaning** before booking [1].

**Additional reminder:** Before confirming either appointment, the front desk should verify the BlueWave patient's current assignment to our office on the BlueWave portal, since assignments can change monthly [5]. And be sure to book each patient's next recall appointment before they leave; patients without a booked recall go on the "Unscheduled Recall" list, which the front desk calls every Wednesday [3].

Since the patient is more than 15 minutes late for a hygiene (cleaning) visit and must be rescheduled, this counts as a late cancellation and the late cancellation fee applies [1]. For a hygiene appointment, the late cancellation fee is **$35** [3].

So you would charge the patient **$35**.

Note: Fees can be waived once per patient per calendar year at the front desk's discretion, or are always waived in cases of medical emergencies or county-declared severe weather [3].

The main phone number for Lakeside Family Dental is **(407) 555-0142** [3].

Our office hours on Friday are 7:30 AM to 1:00 PM [1]. Please note that on the last Friday of each month, the office closes early at 11:00 AM for a staff meeting [3].

Additionally, the front desk does not answer phones from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM, though since Friday closes at 1:00 PM, this applies to the final hour of business [2].

The fee for a no-show (when a patient does not arrive and does not call) is **$75** [1]. Please note that this fee may be waived once per patient per calendar year at the front desk's discretion, and is always waived in cases of medical emergencies or county-declared severe weather [1].

After **three** no-shows within 12 months, the three-strike rule is triggered [1]. Once triggered, the patient may only book same-day appointments for the next 6 months [1]. Any exception to this restriction must be approved by the office manager [1].
New patients should arrive **15 minutes early** for their first visit [1].

The Lakeside Smile Club is an in-house membership for patients without insurance that costs **$29 per month** or **$299 per year** [2]. It covers 2 cleanings, 2 exams, 1 set of bitewing X-rays per year, and includes 20% off other treatment [2].

For our in-house payment plan, you'll need to put **25% down**, and the remaining balance is split over a maximum of **6 months**, interest-free [1]. This plan is available for treatment over $500 [1].
Patients' records requests are fulfilled within **15 business days** [1].
The after-hours voicemail gives the on-call doctor's pager number: (407) 555-0177 [1].

For a knocked-out permanent tooth, the patient should get to the office within **60 minutes** [1]. In the meantime, they should pick up the tooth by the crown (not the root), rinse it gently, and either try to place it back in the socket or keep it in milk [1]. A knocked-out permanent tooth is classified as a dental emergency [3].

A minor aged **14 to 17** may attend a routine cleaning alone (after the first visit) if a signed **Minor Attendance Form** is on file [1]. Please note that a parent or guardian must still be present for the first visit and for any treatment involving numbing, extractions, or sedation [1].
The SunCoast Dental PPO annual maximum is **$1,500 per person** [1].
Claims for SunCoast Dental PPO must be filed within **90 days** of the date of service [2]. As a reminder, we submit claims electronically the same day as the appointment [1].
A BlueWave Dental HMO patient's copay for a porcelain crown (D2740) is **$450** [1].

No, Lakeside Family Dental is **out of network** with GuardStar Dental PPO [1]. We do see patients with GuardStar, but as an out-of-network provider [1]. For reference, we are in network with SunCoast Dental PPO, BlueWave Dental HMO, and the SunState Kids program, and we see patients with other plans—including GuardStar—as out of network [6].

As an out-of-network patient with GuardStar, you would pay our full office fee at the time of service [5]. GuardStar pays the patient directly for out-of-network claims, and we file the claim on your behalf as a courtesy [4][5]. Your coverage would be up to $1,000 per person annually, with a $75 deductible, and 80%/60%/40% coverage for preventive/basic/major services respectively, based on GuardStar's allowed amount [1].

I'd recommend asking for a printed fee estimate before any treatment over $300 so you can budget for the difference between our fee and what GuardStar may reimburse [5].
The standard lab turnaround time for a crown is **10 business days** [2].

We bill the crown (D2740) on the **seat date**, not the prep date. Insurance pays on the date the crown is permanently placed [1]. This is also noted in the office's CDT code reference, which specifies "bill on seat date" for D2740 [6].
The self-pay price for bitewing X-rays is $65 [1].
Nitrous oxide (laughing gas) costs **$55 per visit** [1].
If a new patient's blood pressure is above **180/110**, we do not provide treatment that day and refer them to their physician [2].

For a two-surface MO filling on a back tooth, we use **D2392** (tooth-colored filling, two surfaces, back tooth) [1]. The office notes specifically confirm that "a two-surface filling like 'MO' uses D2392, not D2391" [1].

When submitting the claim, make sure to include the tooth number and both surfaces (M and O), as those are required fields for fillings [5].

The main difference between D4341 and D4342 is the number of teeth being treated in a quadrant:

- **D4341** – Deep cleaning (scaling and root planing) for **4 or more teeth** in a quadrant [1].
- **D4342** – Deep cleaning (scaling and root planing) for **1 to 3 teeth** in a quadrant [1].

Both codes require a quadrant designation (UR, UL, LR, or LL) on the claim [1][5], and both require full periodontal charting showing pocket depths of 4 mm or more, plus X-rays from the last 12 months as a supporting attachment [1][6].

The self-pay fees also differ: D4341 is **$245 per quadrant**, while D4342 is **$175 per quadrant** [1].

Otherwise, they follow the same insurer rules—most plans allow the procedure once per quadrant every 24 months [1].

For a self-pay patient needing a crown and a core buildup, the total office fee is **$1,545** [1].

That breaks down as:

- **Crown:** $1,250 [1]
- **Core buildup:** $295 [1]

I'd also let the patient know that if they'd like to split the payment, we do offer an in-house plan for treatment over $500, which requires 25% down and allows up to 6 months to pay the balance [2].
The office is open on the **first and third Saturday of each month** from 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM, and only **hygiene appointments** are offered on those days [1].

Based on our records, the in-network plans that require **6 months between cleanings** are:

- **BlueWave Dental HMO** – cleanings are covered 2 per year, at least 6 months apart [4].
- **SunState Kids** – also requires 6 months between cleanings [1].

This is different from **SunCoast PPO**, which simply counts 2 cleanings per calendar year and does not have a 6-month gap requirement [1][4].

Before booking any cleaning, we check the patient's specific plan's frequency rule to confirm coverage [1][3]. If the visit falls too soon after the last cleaning for the plan's rules, we let the patient know the self-pay fee ($120 adult cleaning) before scheduling [1].

SunCoast Dental PPO covers a full-mouth or panoramic X-ray once every **5 years** [2]. BlueWave Dental HMO covers full-mouth X-rays once every **3 years** [1]. So BlueWave allows them more frequently — every 3 years versus SunCoast's every 5 years.

Under **SunCoast Dental PPO**, a crown on the same tooth can be replaced once every **5 years** [1]. Under **GuardStar Dental PPO**, a crown on the same tooth can be replaced once every **7 years** [2]. So SunCoast allows replacement more frequently (every 5 years) compared to GuardStar (every 7 years).

Lakeside Family Dental is in network with **SunCoast Dental PPO**, **BlueWave Dental HMO**, and the **SunState Kids program** [1]. SunCoast Dental PPO is confirmed as in network in their plan summary as well [5]. Patients with other plans, such as GuardStar Dental PPO, are seen as out of network [3].

For **SunCoast Dental PPO**, the per-person deductible is **$50** (waived for preventive visits) [2].

For **GuardStar Dental PPO**, the per-person deductible is **$75** [1].

So SunCoast's per-person deductible is $25 lower than GuardStar's, and SunCoast also waives the deductible entirely for preventive services like exams, cleanings, and X-rays [2].

SunCoast Dental PPO covers adult bitewing X-rays at a frequency of **1 set per calendar year** [3]. In comparison, GuardStar Dental PPO covers adult bitewing X-rays at a frequency of **1 set every 2 years** [2].

So SunCoast allows bitewing X-rays twice as often as GuardStar for adults.

Yes, a pre-authorization is required, and there are **two** reasons:

1. **SunCoast PPO plan requirement:** SunCoast requires a pre-authorization for any single treatment over **$400** [5]. Since this crown is $1,250, it far exceeds that threshold.

2. **Our office policy:** Regardless of the insurer, our internal policy mandates a pre-authorization for any treatment plan over **$1,000**, even if the insurer doesn't require one, so the patient knows their estimated cost before treatment [2].

So both the plan rules and our office rules call for a pre-authorization on this crown. Once the doctor finalizes the treatment plan in ChairSide PM, we submit the pre-authorization electronically with the same attachments a claim would need, and most insurers respond within **2 to 4 weeks** [4]. We'd never guess the patient's cost—we wait for the insurer's response and then call the patient to review their estimated cost and schedule [1][4].

Yes, we still send a pre-authorization. Since this plan is $1,200, it meets that threshold.

No, we cannot bill a porcelain crown for a SunState Kids patient on a back molar. Porcelain crowns on back teeth are explicitly **not covered** under the SunState Kids program. Instead, **stainless steel crowns are covered** in that situation [3].

If the patient or family would prefer a porcelain crown, they would need to pay out-of-pocket, as SunState Kids covers exams, cleanings, X-rays, fluoride, sealants, fillings, and simple extractions, but excludes cosmetic treatment and porcelain crowns on posterior teeth [3].

Yes! Fluoride is covered for your 15-year-old under SunCoast Dental PPO. The plan covers fluoride for patients **under age 16**, up to **twice per year** [2]. Our billing notes also confirm the SunCoast age limit for fluoride (code D1206) is under 16 [4].

So your teenager is within the covered age range, and you'll have two fluoride applications per year under the plan.

For a GuardStar patient needing a $400 filling, here's how we handle payment:

1. **Collect the full fee at the time of service.** Because GuardStar is an out-of-network plan, GuardStar pays the **patient** directly rather than the office, so we collect the entire $400 from the patient and provide them with a claim form to submit to GuardStar [1].

2. **No waiting periods** apply under the GuardStar plan, so the claim can be submitted right away [1].

3. **No in-house payment plan is available** for this treatment. Our in-house financing option requires treatment to be over $500, and a $400 filling falls below that threshold [4][6].

4. The patient will then submit the claim form to GuardStar and receive reimbursement directly from the insurer, at which point any amount GuardStar pays them reduces their out-of-pocket cost [1].

If the patient has questions about how much GuardStar will cover, I'd recommend they contact GuardStar directly or check with the office manager, as our sources don't specify GuardStar's exact benefit percentages for fillings.

For a $4,000 treatment plan, we have a couple of great options for paying over time:

**In-House Payment Plan:** Since the treatment is over $500, you qualify for our in-house plan. You'd put down 25% ($1,000) and split the remaining $3,000 over a maximum of 6 months, completely interest-free [3].

**Third-Party Financing (BrightPay Health):** Because your treatment is over $3,000, you also qualify for our third-party financing partner, BrightPay Health, which offers plans over 12 to 24 months [3]. This would give you more time to spread out the payments.

**A few other things worth mentioning:**

- If you don't have insurance, you might also want to ask about our **Lakeside Smile Club** membership ($29/month or $299/year), which covers 2 cleanings, 2 exams, 1 set of bitewing X-rays per year, and gives you 20% off other treatment [5][2].
- If you *did* decide to pay the full $4,000 in advance, there's a 5% discount available (this can't be combined with insurance) [5].
